sessions.description: Sharding is easy. Resharding under heavy load is notoriously difficult. How do you move gigabytes of state across live database nodes without dropping keys, blocking the main event loop, or breaking client abstractions?

sessions.title: APIs That Can't Afford to Be Wrong: Lessons from Moving Money
sessions.track: Modern API Design for Humans and Agents
sessions.description: Most API design advice assumes a forgiving environment: retries are cheap, data has a single source of truth, and a slow response is only an inconvenience. Financial infrastructure assumes none of that. Card networks give you three seconds to auth or decline.

sessions.title: The Freeze Paradox: Why Stopping Deployments Doesn't Stop Failures
sessions.track: Resilience Engineering: Everything Fails All the Time
sessions.description: When systems fail at Netflix and in an environment this complex, they sometimes will, the instinctive response is to freeze deployments.

sessions.title: Legacy vs. AI-Native Is the Wrong Question: Architecting the Modern Platform
sessions.description: Engineering leaders modernizing operational platforms are often presented with a false binary: choose the control and reliability of established enterprise platforms or embrace AI-native tools optimized for speed, automation, and intelligent experiences.

sessions.title: Model-Harness Co-Training: Data-Driven Optimization Toward Pareto-Optimal Agents
sessions.description: Teams with agents in production are chasing the optimal agent. Usually they pick one lever: tune the harness (the prompts, tools, memory, and workflow around the model), or fine-tune the model, but the two depend on each other.

sessions.title: Architecting Nubank's Global Financial Infrastructure
sessions.description: Instant payment frameworks are transforming global finance, but few institutions have faced the infrastructure scale required by Brazil's Pix network.

sessions.title: How Airbnb Guardrailed Its AI Customer Support Agent
sessions.track: Guardrails & Safety Nets (Evals) for the New Landscape

sessions.title: Everything I Knew About Developer Experience Is Wrong for Agents
sessions.track: Modern API Design for Humans and Agents
sessions.description: Most of what we know about developer experience we learned from humans. Agents are a different user, and some of our best practices quietly work against them.

sessions.title: Adapt or Drift: Resilience Engineering When AI Moves the Operating Point
sessions.track: Resilience Engineering: Everything Fails All the Time
sessions.description: Resilient systems do not stay resilient by standing still. They survive by adapting. But adaptation comes with risk: under sustained pressure, organizations and systems can slowly drift toward failure while still appearing to operate normally.

sessions.title: LLM Flip-Flops: From Reliability Risk to a Hill-Climbing Signal
sessions.track: Guardrails & Safety Nets (Evals) for the New Landscape
sessions.description: Run the same task through the same LLM twice, and you may get two materially different answers. This behavior is often dismissed as the stochastic nature of LLMs, but it creates a serious product risk.

sessions.title: The Schema Was Never Enough: The World in Protocols
sessions.track: Modern API Design for Humans and Agents
sessions.description: Every reliable process in the world is a protocol: auctions, double-entry bookkeeping, brokerage account transfers, or APIs. Protocols reduce ambiguity but the world remains messy.

sessions.title: Your Agents Lack Context: Here's How to Fix 'You're absolutely right!"'
sessions.description: Every AI coding tool can generate code. Very few can generate the right code for your organization, because they’re missing context.

sessions.title: Inside the Disaggregated Architecture Serving LLM Inference
sessions.description: Every LLM request is really two very different jobs. Reading your prompt (prefill) is compute-intensive, while generating the response token by token (decode) is dominated by memory bandwidth. For years, the industry ran both phases on the same hardware and accepted the compromise.

sessions.title: No New Backend: The API Layer Behind 800+ Agent-Built Apps at Duolingo
sessions.track: Modern API Design for Humans and Agents
sessions.description: At Duolingo, anyone (engineer or not) can describe an internal tool and get a working app back, deployed against real company systems. That's BuildingHub, and 350 Duolingo employees have created at least one app with it.

sessions.title: Saturation: How Your Software Will Fail at Scale
sessions.track: Resilience Engineering: Everything Fails All the Time
sessions.description: Even in the ethereal world of software, everything has a limit. And, once that limit is reached, very bad things can happen. In this talk, we will explore the problem of saturation: when a software system runs into one of these limits.

sessions.title: Wait, You're Still Doing PRs?
sessions.description: PRs were built for open source. A non-maintainer wanted to contribute, a maintainer needed a gate, and you opened the PR early so the two of you could work through the change together while it was still forming. That was the point. The PR was where the thinking happened.

sessions.title: The Context Gap: Why Correct Agents Fail
sessions.description: Two agents edit different files. Git merges clean. The program is broken. No conflict was thrown, because the collision was in meaning, not in text — and business decisions are almost all semantic.

sessions.title: What Is Incident Severity, but a Lie Agreed Upon?
sessions.track: Resilience Engineering: Everything Fails All the Time
sessions.description: Is your incident severity a complex word problem? Do you arbitrate which severity an incident should be during the incident itself? Do you know what the difference between your severities are? Do you even have incident severity in your org?

sessions.title: AI Amplifies Everything, Including Your Mess: Lessons from Delivering with AI at Global Scale
sessions.description: AI doesn’t fix how a team works. It multiplies it. This talk shares real lessons from an engineering team rebuilding its software development lifecycle around AI while delivering Nu Global, a product that scales financial services globally on top of crypto rails.

sessions.title: Stop Fighting the Remodel: API Design for Models That Outgrew Their Boundaries
sessions.track: Modern API Design for Humans and Agents
sessions.description: Every domain model has a breaking point. At Netflix, ours arrived all at once—Ads, Games, Live events, and entirely new kinds of content. Each pulled the core entities in different, sometimes contradictory directions.

sessions.title: It's Never the Thing That Broke: Learning From Incidents at (AI) Speed
sessions.track: Resilience Engineering: Everything Fails All the Time
sessions.description: When something breaks, our first instinct is to focus on the thing that failed. But in complex systems, the failure is usually the result of many things going right, changing, and interacting in ways we didn't anticipate.

sessions.title: Apache Spark: Structured Streaming Real-Time Mode
sessions.description: Apache Spark Structured Streaming is a distributed stream processing engine built on Spark SQL and is widely used for ETL-style workloads, where seconds- to minutes-level latency is acceptable. But millisecond-latency use cases have historically been out of reach.

sessions.title: Orderly Keys, Wild Values: Adaptive Compression for Distributed Key-Value Storage
sessions.description: At Netflix scale - billions of requests per day and petabytes of key-value data - even small inefficiencies in storage and network paths become expensive.

sessions.title: Skills, Memory, or Fine-Tuning? The Engineering Loop Behind Self-Improving Agents
sessions.description: As agents become mainstream, everyone wants to improve theirs either by making fewer mistakes on existing tasks or by taking on harder ones. This usually happens once an agent is already deployed in production.

sessions.title: Nobody Knows Everything (and That's OK): Building Alignment in Complex, Rapidly Changing Environments
sessions.description: Successful Staff+ engineers build alignment across organizational and technical boundaries, including domains where they aren't the deepest expert.

sessions.title: Breaking Down the Walls to Python & Big Data + AI Performance with Transpilation and LLMs
sessions.description: Many of us have a love hate relationship with Apache Spark, especially when it comes to PySpark. Especially in Python, the UDF performance can be a dumpster fire.

sessions.title: Feeling Faster Isn’t a Metric: Measuring AI’s Real Engineering Impact
sessions.description: AI adoption in engineering is settled. In GitKraken’s 2026 State of AI in Engineering survey of 554 developers and engineering leaders, 96% of teams had adopted AI coding tools and 84% of developers said they feel more productive. Only about one in five can actually measure the impact.

sessions.title: How to Build Online Systems with Object Storage
sessions.description: “Diskless” systems that delegate durability to object storage are everywhere, and for three good reasons:

sessions.title: Inside Asimov: BlackRock’s Platform Architecture for Applied AI at Scale
sessions.description: BlackRock’s Portfolio Management Group is transforming how investment teams conduct research by combining deep investment expertise with shared AI capabilities.

sessions.title: Use AI to Multiply Your Team as a Staff Engineer
sessions.description: Most "AI for engineers" content is about typing faster. That's IC-level work. Staff engineers have a different question to answer. When AI raises the floor on what every engineer can ship, what is the staff engineer's job, and where does the leverage actually come from now?

sessions.title: Building a Data Platform with AI
sessions.description: Data platform sits at the intersection of infrastructure, governance, operations, and user experience.

sessions.title: Notes From 300 Installs Inside Someone Else's Cloud
sessions.description: We run our storage and query backend inside our customers' own VPCs. They own the infrastructure. We own the pager. I'm the person who helps installs it, so I've watched this architecture meet a few hundred different production Kubernetes environments and I've kept notes on what went wrong.

sessions.title: Autoscaling 800 Valkey Clusters: Distributed Systems Lessons from Scaling Stateful Fleets
sessions.description: Autoscaling stateless services is a solved problem. In a sharded datastore, a resize is not a capacity change — it's moving ownership of key ranges between nodes while the cluster serves live traffic, and rebalancing takes long enough that reacting to a traffic peak is already too late.

sessions.title: The Revenge of the Data Scientist: Why Reliable AI Needs Evals, Traces, and Metrics
sessions.description: Most teams can now ship an AI prototype by calling a foundation-model API. The hard part is knowing whether that system works when real users, messy data, and business consequences arrive.

sessions.title: Scaling Tech by Aligning Humans
sessions.description: Scaling a complex technology can get messy without a clear north star or a shared technical strategy. Product strategies from different functions can each deliver impact but may lead to disconnected solutions or inadvertently introduce various forms of technical debt.

sessions.title: One Does Not Simply Add Synchronous Writes - Bridging Batch and Real Time with Apache Iceberg
sessions.description: What happens when a batch ingestion platform needs to behave like an operational database? Datadog’s Reference Tables product was designed for asynchronous uploads of large datasets, but customers increasingly needed synchronous row-level edits, without sacrificing batch scale.

sessions.title: Why Your Document AI Fails in Production — And How to Fix the Infrastructure Underneath It
sessions.description: The session explains why document AI that works in demos can fail in production: document structure can be lost during ingestion, rendering can break on edge cases, and extraction can vary across runs. When agents make routing or approval decisions, teams also need governance.

sessions.title: Lessons from Building a $100M Product in Six Weeks at OpenAI
sessions.description: Engineering is shifting from synchronous, line-by-line implementation to an asynchronous model in which agents execute, verify, and retry while humans own intent, architecture, constraints, and release decisions.

sessions.title: Transitioning From a Startup to a Mature Platform
sessions.description: What you need to succeed in a startup with zero customers is different from what you need when you have a few thousand, and this changes many times as the company grows. Some of these changes are code and architectural changes, some are organizational changes, and some are mindset shifts.

sessions.title: Building a StreamHouse: Turning Kafka Streams into a Millisecond Query Layer
sessions.description: AI agents have compressed business decisions from minutes to seconds. Data systems need to keep up.

sessions.title: Trust, but Verify: Delivering Quality with Agentic Workflows
sessions.description: In spite of all the recent panic, nothing has really changed about software development. We’re worried about agents being unreliable. Newsflash: human devs are too. We’re worried about agents producing more code than we can read, but did you ever really do all your reviews within 24 hours?

sessions.title: When Your Users Are Agents: Lessons from a Distributed Postgres Platform
sessions.description: Distributed systems are built around assumptions about workload behavior: connections have reasonable lifetimes, retries eventually stop, traffic spikes have recognizable causes, and application code produces somewhat predictable query patterns.

sessions.title: Bridging Retrieval and Ranking: From LLM Embeddings and Graph Features to a GPU-Served DLRM
sessions.description: The LinkedIn Feed retrieval layer selects, within 120 ms, the handful of posts each member sees from hundreds of millions of candidates. This split-second decision shapes what over a billion professionals read and engage with every day.

sessions.title: Learning What’s Already There: A Breadth-Based Approach To Onboarding
sessions.description: When onboarding to a new organization, it's vital to bootstrap your network and context quickly.

sessions.title: From Datasets to Data Products: Powering Trusted AI for Social Impact
sessions.description: When an AI agent acts on a nonprofit's behalf, it's only as trustworthy as the data underneath it. At Blackbaud, we build software for the social impact sector, and nonprofits have relied on our data for decades.

sessions.title: Your Agents Have Amnesia: Lessons from Building a Memory Layer for Multi-Agent Systems
sessions.description: Multi-agent systems have a data problem nobody warns you about. Agent B sees Agent A's final output and nothing else; the reasoning, the dead ends, and whatever Agent A figured out three steps in all get thrown away.

sessions.title: Adaptive Systems in Production: What Recommendation Systems Can Teach Us About Agents
sessions.description: As organizations race to build AI agents, many teams are encountering challenges that feel new: evaluation uncertainty, feedback loops, behavioral drift, exploration versus exploitation, and maintaining user trust in systems that continuously adapt.But these challenges are not new.

sessions.title: Failing in Layers: Lessons from Rebuilding Netflix's ML Serving Platform
sessions.description: Everyone talks about model quality. Fewer people talk about what happens when that model has to serve real traffic without falling over, or why the system ended up shaped the way it did in the first place.

sessions.title: Iceberg V4: The Next Chapter in Table Formats
sessions.description: Apache Iceberg V3 adoption is growing and the community is already shaping what comes next. This talk walks through the emerging scope and priorities for the V4 table spec and progress of the proposals currently underway.

sessions.title: How Netflix Retrofitted Its SDLC for AI Coding Agents
sessions.track: Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop
sessions.description: Agentic tools amplify what’s already in the codebase. The agent works through your code, your architecture decisions, and the documentation around them. It follows what it can read and guesses at the rest.

sessions.title: Features vs Futures
sessions.description: Details coming soon.

sessions.title: Platform Engineering’s Second Act: From Vending Machine to Passport Control
sessions.description: Three years ago on the QCon SF stage, I made the case for “Acceleration, Autonomy, and Accountability” as the pillars of a successful platform. Those pillars haven't moved. AI has just rewritten what each one requires, and the platform team's job along with it.

sessions.title: Builder-Driven Development: Rebuilding the Organization Around the Builder
sessions.description: Most teams still run agent development the way they run traditional software projects. Requirements are written up front, builders execute against them, and a demo closes out the cycle. That model works poorly for agents, because the most useful information rarely comes from a planning document.

sessions.title: Simulating the Universe, 100 Times Over: Engineering Highly- Concurrent Agent Testing
sessions.description: Testing AI agents properly is surprisingly hard. Production data sources are moving targets, static datasets go stale, and pointing agents at real systems is risky and impossible to reproduce.

sessions.title: Making Production Legible to Agents: Lessons From Building an Observability MCP
sessions.track: Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop
sessions.description: An agent that can query production telemetry can test its own hypotheses against reality, rather than hallucinate fictions. Observability tooling allows our agents to close the loop and benefit from production wisdom.

sessions.title: No More Small Systems, How AI May Bring Large System Problems to Everyone
sessions.description: Once you figure out how to use AI to make your organization productive, you will soon find you have a whole new set of problems. While some of those problems will be novel thanks to LLMs, many of them are just the result of there being "more stuff".

sessions.title: Beyond the Kubernetes API: Building LinkedIn’s Compute Platform
sessions.description: LinkedIn’s Kubernetes-based compute platform spans more than 500k bare-metal machines, 5M pods, with thousands of developers doing more than 110k deploys a week. We don’t expose raw Kubernetes to developers and instead, provide a curated set of platform offerings.

sessions.title: Legacy as Leverage: How Brownfield Work Builds Technical Judgment
sessions.description: Legacy systems are often treated as a necessary evil: work to be endured before moving on to more “real, strategic” projects.

sessions.title: The Men in Black Know What's in Your JavaScript and How to Fix it!
sessions.description: Ever wonder what’s lurking in the dark corners of your node_modules, like unidentified flying dependencies sneaking aboard your project? In an age of escalating software supply chain attacks, knowing exactly what you're shipping is as vital as tracking strange lights in the sky.

sessions.title: Efficient GPU Agents: Infra for Autonomous LLM Perf Optimization
sessions.track: Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop
sessions.description: Parasail serves open-weight LLMs on distributed clusters of GPUs managed by Kubernetes. The typical performance optimization loop is to reproduce a problem or measure a regression, iterate on code or config, set up and run benchmarks, and decide whether the change is worth shipping.

sessions.title: Growing Engineers in the Era of Agentic Coding
sessions.description: Early-career engineers are learning the craft in an environment where the surface they touch is often an agent, not a codebase. The instinct is to treat this as a rupture in how engineers grow. It isn't.

sessions.title: Observability: The Missing Control Plane for Agentic Engineering
sessions.description: As AI agents move from generating code to testing, deploying, and operating it, the important question is no longer “How autonomous is the agent?” It’s “What can this agent safely decide without a human?”

sessions.title: The Death of the Code Review
sessions.description: Code review was built for a world where humans wrote all the code.

sessions.title: Dreams on Paper: How Agents Learn from Experience
sessions.track: Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop
sessions.description: Agents produce high-fidelity traces of everything they do. But traces alone don't produce memory. This talk introduces three primitives for turning session history into something actionable:

sessions.title: Shipping Faster, Understanding Less
sessions.description: AI is changing software development faster than our engineering practices are evolving, and yet many teams are facing growing pressure to ship features faster. But moving faster can create three related threats to software health: technical debt, cognitive debt, and intent debt.

sessions.title: Why Most Platform Teams Fail: The Adoption Problem Nobody Wants to Own
sessions.description: We have all seen the moment: the platform goes live, the launch deck looks sharp, the portal is polished, the golden paths are documented, and yet teams quietly continue doing things the old way. Not always because the platform is bad, but because adoption was assumed, not owned.

sessions.title: You Can't Read the Code Anymore - Verifying Software in the Age of AI
sessions.description: AI writes most of the code now, so the hard part of engineering has moved from authoring to the part we’re worse at - verifying. With the incentives all pushing toward shipping faster and faster - the rational move is to skim the diff, click through a little manual QA, and ship on vibes.

sessions.title: Avoiding Prompt Debt & Other Context Failures
sessions.track: Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop
sessions.description: As agents evolve, prompts get unruly. Edge cases are patched with one-line hotfixes, or with stacked instructions of escalating severity when an issue proves stubborn. Over time, those instructions pile up into a brittle artifact, overfit to an aging model.

sessions.title: The Diary of an AI Adopter: How I Went From Skeptical to Enthusiastic in Our Organization’s AI Migration Efforts
sessions.description: From market research reporting questionable success of AI adoption in enterprise, to CEOs announcing layoffs due to AI, to companies announcing they’re cutting back or eliminating AI due to prohibitive costs or technical missteps, it can be hard to know what the path to success should look like.

sessions.title: Building a Migration Platform: Moving 100+ Netflix RDBMS Workloads to Aurora PostgreSQL
sessions.description: In late 2024, Netflix made a bet: consolidate the vast majority of our relational database use cases onto a single engine: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.

sessions.title: When Everyone Can Code, Who Owns Production?
sessions.description: AI is making it dramatically easier to create and change software, but writing code is only one part of the software lifecycle. Every change still needs to be deployed, observed, operated, diagnosed, and kept reliable in production.
